findings.title: install.cmd reports success when the library replacement is killed half-way
findings.what: install.ps1 step 4 deletes the old library file by file (Remove-Item -Recurse) after copying the new one to library.new. On this PC the PowerShell process was terminated in the middle of that delete: exit code 0 to cmd and to the caller, no catch, no finally, nothing printed after «Панель:». The library is left half-deleted and library.new orphaned; the panel then shows a broken catalogue until a rerun.
findings.cause: Almost certainly 360 Total Security, which runs on the build PC (QHActiveDefense, 360webshield; SecurityCenter2 lists only a disabled Defender): its behaviour protection kills a script that writes many media files and then deletes many .jpg/.mp4 — the pattern of a ransomware. Evidence: a bare script with only Remove-Item (or [IO.Directory]::Delete) of a copy of the library, nothing held open, run with powershell -File from Git Bash, dies at the same point every time — right after the third .jpg of LOGO_Mark (19 of 169 files deleted), exit 0, no finally, no transcript footer. Through install.cmd from the PowerShell tool a plain reinstall into a sandbox, nothing held, dies the same way. powershell -Command "& install.ps1", node rmSync and rm -rf delete the same tree without being stopped. No readable 360 log names the kill.
findings.whyItMatters: Office PCs of the users carry antivirus or EDR too; any of them may stop the installer the same way, and the user is told nothing.
suggestedFix: Swap the library by renames, not by a delete: rename library to library.old-<time>, rename library.new to library, then remove library.old-* last and best-effort (a failure there is a warning; the next install retries). A directory rename is one operation, also refuses at once when a file inside is open, before anything is lost.
Do the same for the CEP folder (step 3).

Make the caller see an interrupted run: install.ps1 writes a completion marker as its very last step (e.g. installed.txt with a run id that install.cmd passes in); install.cmd checks it after powershell returns and, when it is missing, prints «Установка прервана (возможно, её остановил антивирус). Запустите установщик ещё раз.» and exits 1. Same check in install.command for parity.
Installer stand: a case where install.ps1 is killed between the copy and the swap (e.g. a test hook that exits the process) must end with exit 1 and an intact old or new library.

findings.title: A file held open in the old library leaves the same half-deleted state, with an error
findings.what: Sandbox, one preview held open by another process (FileShare.Read): through powershell -Command the installer prints «ОШИБКА: Процесс не может получить доступ к файлу "preview.mp4", так как этот файл используется другим процессом.» and exits 1 — correct — but by then every item before LOGO_Mark is already deleted and library.new stays. Who can hold a preview: a panel still playing it, or a CEP engine that outlives its host for a few seconds. The rename swap of finding 1 fixes this too.
findings.repro: install.ps1 -Sandbox <dir> twice; before the second run open <dir>\ProgramData\CloudRuBrandKit\library\items\LOGO_Mark\preview.mp4 with [IO.File]::Open(path, 'Open', 'Read', 'Read').
